public_holidays: No state-only statutory public holidays: Austria's public holidays are national and are on Austria's record.
culture-cycles.note: The patron-saint day is a school holiday in this state. The ministry lists it apart from the statutory public holidays, so do not assume shops or businesses close; the ministry page does not say.

laws.rule: Burgenland charges a visitor tax (Ortstaxe) of EUR 4.50 per person per day of paid accommodation (about A$7.15 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026), under section 21(1) of the Burgenländisches Tourismusgesetz 2021. It also applies to people staying overnight in a motorhome or caravan on parking areas (section 20(3)). Children up to 18 are exempt (section 20(4)). The amount is indexed to consumer prices when the index moves by 10% or more (section 21(3)); the state publishes the current tariff by 15 February each year.
laws.heading: Bgld. TG 2021, paragraphs 20 and 21

laws.rule: Burgenland: Curfew for minors in public places and at public events (the Jugendschutz rule): young people up to the end of their 14th year may be out only from 05:00 to 23:00, and up to the end of their 16th year only from 05:00 to 01:00, unless they have an accompanying person or a justified reason such as heading home (section 8 of the Burgenländisches Jugendschutzgesetz 2002).
laws.heading: Bgld. Jugendschutzgesetz 2002, section 8

laws.rule: Burgenland: under 16, buying, having or drinking alcohol in public places and at public events is banned; under 18 the same applies to drinks with distilled alcohol (above 0.5% alcohol) and to tobacco products as listed in the federal TNRSG (section 11(1)).
laws.heading: Bgld. Jugendschutzgesetz 2002, section 11
